name: Robinson R22
summary: Tiny two-seat piston helicopter that dominates US primary helicopter flight training and is also used for ranch and private flying.

wings: Two-blade teetering main rotor on a tall, slender mast with a small fairing
engines: Piston engine mounted low behind the seats, largely exposed in an open frame
Cooling fan shroud and exhaust visible below the mast
fuselage: Very small bubble cabin with one door per side and only two seats
Overall tiny size relative to people standing next to it
tail: Small two-blade tail rotor with upper and lower vertical fins and a small horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Only one door per side on a tiny two-seat bubble cabin
Engine and frame largely exposed below the rotor mast
Very thin two-blade rotor on a tall slender mast

confusedWith.howToTell: The R22 is smaller with one door per side and an open engine bay; the R44 has two doors per side, four seats and a cowled engine.
The R22 has a two-blade rotor and an unbraced tubular boom; the Schweizer/Hughes 300 has three blades and a boom held up by struts.
The Bell 47 has an open lattice (truss) tail boom and a fishbowl canopy; the R22 has an enclosed tubular boom and a pointed cabin.
The Cabri G2 has three blades and a ducted tail fan in the fin; the R22 has a two-blade teetering rotor and an exposed tail rotor.
The Enstrom 280 has a three-blade rotor and a wider three-seat egg-shaped canopy; the R22 has a thin two-blade rotor and only two seats.
The Brantly B-2 has three narrow rotor blades and a vertical engine behind its bubble; the R22 has a two-blade teetering rotor.
